title: O2 unit failure: Astronaut 3 exercising
purpose: O2 production stops and cabin PIO2 leaves normoxia (145). While Ece exercises her SpO2 drops and a personal hypoxia decision is raised; exercise pulse does not count as evidence. Personal pulse deviation in the same scenario: Ayşe's and Mert's pulse are both 80; Ayşe baseline 64 → +16 Watch, Mert baseline 67 → +13 normal. Same pulse, different baseline, different decision. Red when cabin PIO2 falls below 127.
baseline_note: mean values come from ranges.json vital_karar_parametreleri.baz_cizgi. sd is simulator noise only (assumption; the decision rule does not use sd, it uses a fixed difference). hrv_rmssd and blood pressure are not in ranges.json (assumption).

pp_o2.note: equivalent of PIO2 149 mmHg (middle of normoxia 145–155): 149 × 760/713 mmHg

model.note: ranges.json (PR #16 v1.1) values. Before the failure, life support is regulated (net 0): production covers consumption, removal covers production, cabin values stay constant; only the failing gas moves. Volume 75 m³. Times are aligned with the #14 atmosphere engine in the same model (regulated profile); tests/test_scenarios.py compares the cabin series with the engine.
model.measurement_note: Measurement interval is 5 mission minutes (demo: 0.5 real seconds, time multiplier 600); 3 consecutive measurements = 15 mission minutes.

cabin_pio2_low_critical.condition: cabin PIO2 < 127 (lower limit of mild hypoxia)

crew_hypoxia_caution.condition: SpO2 drop ≥ 3 AND cabin PIO2 < 145; when resting, additionally pulse or respiration rise ≥ watch

proposed_rules.exercise_rule: During exercise, pulse and respiration rises count neither as an alarm nor as hypoxia evidence (user rule). The ranges.json olasi_hipoksi condition includes this exception (#21): pulse/respiration rise is only looked for in a resting person.

events.note: The O2 production unit stops; consumption continues according to pulse.
While Ayşe rests, her pulse rises from her own baseline of 64 to 80 (+16): cardiac load Watch. Same pulse as Mert (80); the baseline difference changes the decision. Unrelated to O2, SpO2 is normal.
Mert's pulse also rises to 80 but his baseline is 67: +13, below the threshold (+15) → normal. Same pulse as Ayşe, different decision.
Ece starts exercising (cabin PIO2 is already below 145). The pulse/respiration rise comes from exercise; it is neither an alarm nor evidence.
During exercise SpO2 drops from 98 to 91.5 (−6.5). Exaggerated for the demo; shown as SIMULATED on screen.

Exercise ends; she moves to rest over 10 minutes (at the 3rd resting measurement the pulse is below the threshold). Pulse +11 is below the cardiac load threshold (+15). Respiration stays +6 at rest: a hypoxia symptom at low cabin PIO2; together with SpO2 −4, Watch continues (resting condition: SpO2 AND respiration/pulse rise). There is no respiration rule in this scenario, so no separate respiration alert is raised.

expected_alerts.why: While Ayşe rests, her pulse is 15 above her own baseline (64) (3 consecutive measurements).
Cabin PIO2 fell below the normoxia range (145–155 mmHg).
expected_alerts.recommendation: Check the O2 unit, prepare backup O2, reduce exertion.

expected_alerts.why: While Ece exercises, her SpO2 dropped 3 points below her own baseline (98); cabin PIO2 is below 145. Exercise pulse was not counted as evidence.
expected_alerts.recommendation: Stop exercise, check the O2 source and cabin PIO2.

expected_alerts.why: Ece's SpO2 dropped 6 points below her baseline; cabin PIO2 is below normoxia.
expected_alerts.recommendation: Stop exercise, switch to backup O2, report to Earth.

expected_alerts.why: Cabin PIO2 fell below 127 mmHg (lower limit of mild hypoxia, Table 6.2-1).
expected_alerts.recommendation: Switch to backup O2, report to Earth.

forbidden_alerts.why: Exercise pulse (130) does not count as cardiac load; rest is reached with a 10 min ramp, and at the 3rd resting measurement (670) the baseline difference is +10.6: below the threshold.
Exercise respiration does not count as an alarm. The +6 at rest is hypoxia evidence only; there is no separate respiration rule in this scenario.
Mert's pulse 80 = his baseline 67 + 13; below the threshold (+15). Same pulse as Ayşe (80), different decision.
Ayşe's pulse rise is not hypoxia; SpO2 is normal.
No personal hypoxia decision for someone without symptoms.

forbidden_evidence.why: Pulse/respiration is not written as hypoxia evidence during exercise.

demo_notes: Ayşe's and Mert's pulse are both 80: Ayşe yellow (baseline 64 → +16), Mert green (baseline 67 → +13). Same pulse, different baseline: the data shows why a personal baseline matters. Seed 42 is fixed, the result is the same on every run.
While Ece's pulse is 130 the system stays quiet and speaks when SpO2 drops: it tells exercise apart.
Ece's personal alert comes long before the cabin turns red: early warning.
